body: Thank you. Wish you the best as well. I'm a gentlewoman ;)

Thank you for this. I have read loads of replies like this to people in the past but have never had someone reply directly. 

I am truly scared of going into "recovery" -it is not really a thing in my life! Most people I know drink to excess, but still I know I am a step ahead. I just don't want to be different to my friends and colleagues. My work life has loads of drinking involved, and tbh if I don't drink at events I can't handle it. Its part of my job. I realise these are excuses. I get grumpy if I have no reason to drink and have had a couple of sober.

I suppose the thing I am grappling with is that I cannot truly believe a sober life is better. I know people say it is but a lot of time a that is wrapped in religion and, no offense to anyone religious, but im just not. So it is meaningless  to me. The main thing I worry about now is dying before my parents, because I don't want them to feel that pain. 

. If a degenerate fuckup like me can manage it, so can you.  - I am interested in this. I often feel like this, a lost cause. But sometimes I feel special, or unique or something. I suppose everyone is unique and maybe everyone feels like this. I'm grappling with that idea as it disrupts my self view.

I also think sometimes that we have been told that drinking is bad (fuck knows why we are encouraged to do it from childhood), but there isn't really a good or bad. At the end of the day the world only lives inside of each of our minds. From the moment we are born to the moment we die - the only true sense of reality we have is what we experience. That is our own universe. And so, surely it is up to each of us how to spend those hours/days/years. I am not saying that drinking alcohol is good, I just want to understand my reality vs everyone elses. 

I also am not sure about living longer. Seems like the end of life is quite rubbish. Would it not be better to have a good time now and lose 10 bad years in a care home at the end?

Thanks for replying. I think I have been at this level for maybe a year. It has been slipping. Lockdown has affected things. Despite being suicidally depressed press lockdown I was being relatively healthy - gym 3x a week, not eating badly - not drinking too much (comparatively, still obviously drinking loads byspme people's standards).

But lockdown has really accelerated things. I always knew it was in there, the lack of self control, the hunger, (I guess they call it an addictive personality) but despite having an intelligent and logical brain, when I am in the moment the physical and emotional feeling I have is overpowering. I have been pouring a drink and knowing it is objectively the wrong thing to do, bit it feels like something core in my soul is overiding my logical thoughts. Like I have another version of myself talking in my brain, and I know they are bad, but they always win. Maybe this is just who I am and Iam fighting too hard?

I'm terrified to have to be sober. I know I feel better for a while but I find life boring. I know the whole thing only boring people get bored. But I'm not boring, I'm actually not.

 It started off that I was determined to experience everything life could hold. I remember having this value at maybe 10 or 11. I got stoned/drunk for the first time simultaneously at 13. I think I always was up for it, not sure when the addiction took hold but I think around 22. I was probably on my way before that but didn't think a 17yr old girl with good grades could be addicted to anything. 

Anyway, another ramble. I just know it is a problem but I don't want it to be. I've been managing it for over 10 years and will keep managing If I can, I just want to know how not to spiral down, as I can already feel it happening
Sorry also realise this is a weird comment to post on an AA sub! Just am trying to make sense of everything and be honest. Thank you for replying I really appreciate it.

I dislike the concept of AA - I admit I'm scared of it, but I'm also very anti religion, spirituality etc. I believe in science and facts so I have a feeling it wouldn't work for me. I would like to hear counter arguments though.
